title: partials: all 21 site-site g(r), chained accumulation
purpose: Exercises `partials`, the EPSR analysis program [@epsrmanual] that computes the intermolecular site-site radial distribution functions g(r) of every pair of atom types of an `.ato` configuration and averages them over successive configurations (`nsumt`). This is how an EPSR user obtains the partial g(r) of the refined model [@soper2005].
system: Analysed configuration: `200DMSO400Water.ato`, an unchanged copy of the EPSR-test box of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO; atom types S, O, C, H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1): 3200 atoms, DMSO mole fraction 1/3, 300 K, cubic box of side 33.1213 Å (0.0881 atoms/Å³), the EPSR model of the deuterated DMSO-water neutron data (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), cf. [@soperluzar1992]. With no centre atom (`atom-c`, `atom-z`, `atom-r` all `*`) the program histograms all intermolecular distances of each of the 6·7/2 = 21 type pairs and divides by the ideal-gas number in each shell, giving g(r) [@hansenmcdonald2006,@allentildesley1987] on 300 points out to half the box side (`rnormalise 1.0`; the reference r grid ends at 16.56 Å).
inputs: `all.PARTIALS.dat` written by hand from the defaults printed by the Fortran program: `nz 300`, `rnormalise 1.0`, `nsumt 0`, `atom-c/z/r *`, `ndist 1` (recomputed by the program); `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied unchanged from EPSR-test.
verification: `repeat 2`: pass 1 starts the accumulation (`nsumt 0`), pass 2 reads `all.PARTIALS.g01` back through `r_int` and forms the running average and spread in `outgofz`. Compared after each pass: `all.PARTIALS.g01` (21 g(r) with their spreads), the rewritten `all.PARTIALS.dat` (the Fortran reference after pass 2 has `nsumt 2`, `ndist 21`) and `fort.14`, the list of the 21 pairs S-S ... H1-H1. The configuration is the same in every pass, so the chained passes test the read-back of the accumulated file and the running-average arithmetic.
notes: `fort.14`: the Fortran writes these lines to unit 14 after `save_files_others` has closed it, so gfortran creates the default file `fort.14`; the port writes the same file.
